page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is an EASv4-family virtual machine configured with 48 virtual CPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 24 physical cores running at 3.525 GHz, the instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, featuring simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 786 GB solid-state drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, as demonstrated by the PassMark CPU encryption test. Memory performance is robust, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, while raw memory bandwidth tests for both small cached and large uncached blocks fall within the average range. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 and image processing workloads also show strong performance, though large-scale LLM text generation using a 70B model represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources, the E48as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The combination of 384 GB of RAM, a 786 GB local SSD, and strong multi-core processing makes this instance well-suited for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application hosting, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
